realDefectFixed.problem: _key() compared the lock file with f.path.endsWith('/.lock'); Windows File.path uses backslashes, so the lock file was treated as 'existing data without a key' and every open threw RouteStoreFailure(keyUnavailable).
realDefectFixed.fix: compare the last path segment via f.uri.pathSegments.last instead of a POSIX suffix
realDefectFixed.platformsAffected: Windows only; Android/iOS (POSIX) were never affected
realDefectFixed.whyItMattered: This line was raising a false signal that looked like a Keychain requirement

wrongDiagnosisCorrected.earlierClaim: 4 route-memory test files were skipped because they require iOS Keychain
wrongDiagnosisCorrected.actualCause: one POSIX-only path comparison plus Windows refusing to delete an open file (errno 32 on .lock)
wrongDiagnosisCorrected.evidence: tearDown/open produced PathAccessException 'Cannot delete file ...\.lock (OS Error: 另一个程序正在使用此文件, errno = 32)'

testHygiene.removed: whole-file skips for captured_route_store_test / encrypted_route_store_test / route_journey_page_test / route_record_replay_test
testHygiene.added: per-test Windows skips only for the 8 cases that delete/corrupt files while the store holds .lock, each labelled with the true cause
testHygiene.effect: Flutter suite went from 457 passed / 4 files skipped to 512 passed / 8 tests skipped

overlayScriptUpdated.section8: now patches the .lock fix and the Windows lock-skip helpers/wrappers instead of Keychain whole-file guards

knownLimitations: The 8 skipped tests exercise deletion of a file the store holds open; Windows forbids it, POSIX allows it. They run in full on macOS/CI.

No Android device or iOS build was available, so no runtime verification of route memory was performed; the storage layer itself is Dart-level (path_provider + flutter_secure_storage) and platform-neutral by construction.
Android route-memory CAPTURE (camera/landmark plugins) is still iOS-only upstream and remains the next real parity gap.
